source: K. Ikeda, 'Demonstration of Quantum Energy Teleportation on Superconducting Quantum Hardware', Phys. Rev. Applied 20, 024051 (2023); arXiv:2301.02666v5 (parent file); IBM Quantum documentation, 'Plans overview', https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/guides/plans-overview (Open Plan budget); IBM Quantum documentation, 'Workload usage', https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/guides/estimate-job-run-time (QPU-time estimate)
location: Sweep grids around the parent file's Table III (ibm_cairo) calibration point; no grid entry other than the multiplier 1 is a published number. Open Plan budget: the IBM 'Plans overview' page, sentence 'up to 10 minutes per 28-day rolling window'
comment: SYNTHETIC sweep axes for papers/hardware-as-noisy-field: dimensionless multipliers applied by vacuum.hardware.noise.scale_calibration to the parent file's sourced numbers (gate errors x nu, readout flips x nu, T1 and T2 / nu). Only nu = 1 is the device; every other point is a simulation choice, chosen to bracket where the two minimal protocols lose their 3-sigma signal. The shot budget is likewise a choice, sized against the Open Plan allowance transcribed here. The tiling of the two Table III rows over an N-qubit register is a modelling choice of vacuum.hardware.noise, not a number from any source.

changes.gate_error_multiplier_grid: new synthetic axis: multiplies the parent's qubit0/qubit1 Pauli-X errors and CNOT error together (relaxation kept at the sourced T1/T2)
changes.readout_error_multiplier_grid: new synthetic axis: multiplies the parent's readout assignment errors (clipped at 0.5)
changes.t1_divisor_grid: new synthetic axis: divides the parent's T1 and T2 (both, so T2 <= 2 T1 is preserved)
changes.shots_per_circuit: simulation choice for the survival analysis (not from the parent, whose runs used 10^5 shots)

gate_error_multiplier_grid.location: none (simulation grid); multiplier 1 = Table III of the parent

readout_error_multiplier_grid.location: none (simulation grid); multiplier 1 = Table III of the parent

t1_divisor_grid.location: none (simulation grid); divisor 1 = Table III of the parent (T1 = 146.43 us / 94.28 us)

open_plan_qpu_budget.location: IBM Quantum documentation, 'Plans overview' (https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/guides/plans-overview), retrieved 2026-09-02: 'up to 10 minutes per 28-day rolling window'
open_plan_qpu_budget.note: 10 minutes of QPU time per 28-day rolling window on the free Open Plan; stated as 600 s. The page lists no shot or circuit limit.

qpu_time_overhead.location: IBM Quantum documentation, 'Workload usage' (https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/guides/estimate-job-run-time), retrieved 2026-09-02: 'If you aren't using any advanced error mitigation techniques or custom rep_delay, you can use 2+0.00035*<num executions> as a quick formula.'
qpu_time_overhead.note: the constant term of the quick formula; QPU time in seconds

qpu_time_per_execution.location: same sentence as qpu_time_overhead; '<num executions> is the total number of circuits times the number of shots, where the circuits are those generated after PUB elements are broadcasted'
qpu_time_per_execution.note: seconds per (circuit x shot); consistent with the stated default rep_delay: 'the default is given by backend.default_rep_delay, which is 250 microseconds on most IBM Quantum backends'
